title: How should 1, 3 and 7 fill the frame for the largest answer?
description: The digits one, three and seven fill a frame of two boxes times one box. The largest digit becomes the multiplier, the other two go in decreasing order, and place value gives the answer. The next best way is checked and found smaller.
teaching_notes: One idea: the largest digit is the multiplier and the other two digits go in decreasing order in the two digit number. Watch for students who make the biggest two digit number first and multiply by the leftover digit.

source: Figure it Out (the largest product, question 1)
video_script.why: The child uses the rule from the solved example: the largest digit multiplies and the others go in decreasing order.
video_script.substitution: Digits 1, 3 and 7: multiplier 7, two digit number 31, multiply by place value, then check the next best way.
video_script.anchor: the frame of two boxes, a times sign and one box, with the digits 1, 3 and 7 to place
video_script.payoff_line: The largest answer is thirty one times seven, which is two hundred seventeen

final_answer.spoken: thirty one times seven, which is two hundred seventeen

maths_rules: largest digit 7 is the multiplier; the other digits 3 and 1 in decreasing order give 31
video_script.design: One idea: the largest digit is the multiplier. The frame stays on the board all video and the check is the last step.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='cards'/>Fill the digits one, three and seven into a two digit number times a one digit number.
<bookmark mark='frame'/>The frame has two boxes, the times sign and one box.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which way gives the largest multiplication answer?

beats.on_screen: the cards and the frame stay on the board while the child thinks

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: arrows run from the one digit box to both boxes of the two digit number

marks.plan: the frame is shown again with the three cards beside it
marks.both: arrows run from the single box to both digits of the two digit number

narration: <bookmark mark='plan'/>We solve it the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='both'/>The one digit multiplier works on both digits of the two digit number. The digit we choose to multiply matters a lot.

beats.on_screen: Given: digits 1, 3, 7, each used once, in (two digit) × (one digit)

marks.given: the digits and the frame are written on the board

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the digits one, three and seven, each used once. They fill a two digit number times a one digit number.

beats.on_screen: To find: the largest multiplication answer

marks.find: the words largest multiplication answer are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the largest multiplication answer.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: the largest digit 7 is the multiplier

marks.seven: the card 7 moves into the single box

beats.colours: the multiplier in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='seven'/>Step one, take the largest digit, seven, as the multiplier. It works on both digits of the other number.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the other digits in decreasing order: 3 then 1, so 31 × 7

marks.three: the card 3 moves into the tens box
marks.one: the card 1 moves into the ones box

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step two, put the other two digits in decreasing order, three first.
<bookmark mark='one'/>That makes the two digit number thirty one.

marks.values: 210 and 7 are written under the two parts

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step three, multiply by place value. Thirty times seven is two hundred ten.
<bookmark mark='values'/>One times seven is seven, and the two parts are added.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, check the next best way: 71 × 3 = (70 × 3) + (1 × 3) = 210 + 3 = 213; 213 is less than 31 × 7
narration: <bookmark mark='next'/>Step four, check the next best way, seventy one times three. Seventy times three is two hundred ten, and one times three is three.
<bookmark mark='less'/>That gives two hundred thirteen, which is smaller.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The largest answer is thirty one times seven, which is two hundred seventeen.
